data.name: AppTitle
data.comment: Window title. "N1MM" and "DXKeeper" are product names - do not translate.

data.name: SettingsHeader
data.comment: Heading of the settings section.

data.name: NetworkHeader
data.comment: Heading of the card holding ports and the multicast group.

data.name: ServicesHeader
data.comment: Heading of the card holding what DXKeeper should do with each logged QSO.

data.name: DiagnosticsHeader
data.comment: Heading of the card holding logging options.

data.name: GeneralHeader
data.comment: Heading of the card holding settings that belong to the gateway itself rather than to what it talks to - currently just the interface language.

data.name: LogCopy
data.comment: Button copying the visible operation log to the clipboard.

data.name: LogClear
data.comment: Button clearing the on-screen operation log. Does not affect ErrorLog.txt.

data.name: LogCopyTip
data.value: Copy the operation log to the clipboard

data.name: LogClearTip
data.value: Clear the on-screen log. ErrorLog.txt is not affected.

data.name: LogCopied
data.value: Operation log copied to the clipboard — {0} lines.
data.comment: {0} is a line count. Written without brackets on purpose: parenthesised text around a placeholder is where the machine pass loses a bracket, and the result renders as ")12 lines". See the note on brackets at the top of this file.

data.name: FailedQsoIndicator
data.comment: Always-present link in the middle of the window footer. Quiet when nothing has failed, highlighted with a count when something has. Keep it SHORT - it sits between two groups of buttons.

data.name: FailedQsoIndicatorCount
data.comment: Same link once QSOs have failed this run. {0} is a count. Keep it short. Written without brackets on purpose - as "Failed QSOs ({0})" the machine pass moved the bracket and returned "(){0})", which reads as "Failed QSOs ()2)". Punctuation wrapped tightly around a placeholder does not survive translation reliably.

data.name: FailedQsoNoneTip
data.value: No QSOs have failed this run. Click to open the folder where they would be saved, in case an earlier run left a file behind.
data.comment: Tooltip when nothing has failed. The second half matters: a file from an earlier run is otherwise easy to miss.

data.name: UdpPortLabel
data.comment: Label for the port N1MM broadcasts QSO data to. "UDP" is a protocol name - do not translate.

data.name: UdpPortTip
data.value: UDP port that N1MM Logger+ broadcasts QSO XML to (default 12060)
data.comment: Tooltip. Keep "N1MM Logger+", "UDP", "QSO" and "XML" in English.

data.name: MulticastLabel
data.comment: Label for an optional IPv4 multicast group address.

data.name: MulticastPlaceholder
data.comment: Placeholder shown inside the empty multicast text box.

data.name: MulticastTip
data.value: Optional. Leave blank unless the sending program is configured to send to a multicast group (224.0.0.0 - 239.255.255.255). Unicast and broadcast are received either way. The group is joined on the interface the routing table selects.
data.comment: Tooltip. Do not translate the address range.

data.name: DxKeeperPortLabel
data.comment: Label. "DXKeeper" and "TCP" - do not translate.

data.name: DxKeeperPortTip
data.value: Read-only here. Set it in DXKeeper: {0}. The gateway sends to Base Port + 1, which is the port DXKeeper shows in that panel's heading.
data.comment: Tooltip. {0} is the English menu path inside DXKeeper (DxKeeperConfigPath) and must stay untranslated, because DXKeeper's own interface is English-only.

data.name: DxKeeperConfigPath
data.value: Config > Defaults tab > Network Service > Base Port
data.comment: DO NOT TRANSLATE. A literal menu path inside DXKeeper, whose interface is English-only. Translating it would describe a menu that does not exist.

data.name: DxKeeperPortReading
data.comment: Placeholder shown until DXKeeper's configured port has been read.

data.name: StatusHeader
data.comment: Heading of the section showing whether each DXLab program is reachable.

data.name: LogHeader
data.comment: Heading of the running list of what the gateway has done.

data.name: SeeErrorLog
data.comment: Link shown when something has been written to the error log. "ErrorLog" is the filename ErrorLog.txt - do not translate.

data.name: DisplayErrorLog
data.comment: Button that opens ErrorLog.txt.

data.name: CheckDxkLookup
data.comment: "QSO" means a radio contact and is used in English worldwide - do not translate.

data.name: CheckDxkLookupTip
data.value: Direct DXKeeper to display previous QSOs with the logged callsign

data.name: CheckCallbook
data.comment: A callbook is a database of licensed operators.

data.name: CheckCallbookTip
data.value: Direct DXKeeper to query its selected callbook

data.name: CheckEqsl
data.comment: "eQSL.cc" is a website name - do not translate.

data.name: CheckEqslTip
data.value: Direct DXKeeper to upload logged QSO to eQSL.cc

data.name: CheckLotw
data.comment: "LoTW" is the ARRL's Logbook of the World - do not translate.

data.name: CheckLotwTip
data.value: Direct DXKeeper to upload logged QSO to LoTW

data.name: CheckClubLog
data.comment: "Club Log" is a website name - do not translate.

data.name: CheckClubLogTip
data.value: Direct DXKeeper to upload logged QSO to Club Log

data.name: WarnUploadTitle
data.value: Uploading each QSO as it is logged
data.comment: Title of the warning shown when Upload to eQSL.cc, LoTW or Club Log is switched on. This read "Uploading as you go" and German rendered it as "uploading as you walk" - "as you go" is an idiom. See the note on idioms at the top of this file.

data.name: WarnUploadMessage
data.value:
WARNING - uploading each QSO to an online logbook as it is logged can have unintended side effects if you later change or delete that QSO.
DXKeeper uploads a QSO as soon as it is logged. If the QSO is edited or deleted afterwards, the gateway removes it from DXKeeper and logs the corrected one - but an upload that has already gone out cannot be recalled. LoTW in particular has no way to delete a QSO you have uploaded, so the original stays there and the correction is added alongside it.
Consider leaving these switched off during a contest and uploading from DXKeeper yourself once the log is final.
See Help, under Change/Delete QSOs and Upload toggles.
data.comment: The whole point of this string. "LoTW", "DXKeeper", "QSO" and the Help section name stay in English. Written without brackets on purpose - see the note on brackets at the top of this file.

data.name: CheckVerboseLoggingTip
data.value: Show low-priority status events in the operation log, such as DDE connecting and disconnecting
data.comment: "DDE" is a Windows protocol name - do not translate. Written without brackets on purpose - see the note on brackets at the top of this file.

data.name: FailedQsoCount
data.comment: Status line. {0} is a count. Followed by links reading "file" and "folder". See FailedQsoCountOne for the singular.

data.name: FailedQsoCountOne
data.comment: Singular form of FailedQsoCount. Languages with more plural forms may need extra keys.

data.name: FailedQsoOpenFile
data.comment: Link that opens the failed-QSO ADIF file.

data.name: FailedQsoOpenFolder
data.comment: Link that shows the failed-QSO file in Explorer.

data.name: FailedQsoTip
data.value:
{0} QSOs were not delivered to DXKeeper this run. Click to show the file in its folder, import it into DXKeeper, then delete it. This count clears when the file is gone.
{1}
data.comment: Tooltip once QSOs have failed. {0} is a count, {1} is the full path of the ADIF file - do not translate the path.

data.name: LanguageLabel
data.comment: Label for the user-interface language selector.

data.name: LanguageTip
data.value: Language of this window. "Follow Windows" uses the Windows display language. A change takes effect the next time the gateway starts.

data.name: LanguageFollowWindows
data.comment: First entry of the language list, meaning "use the Windows display language".

data.name: LanguageRestartNote
data.value: Restart the gateway to switch the interface to {0}.
data.comment: Shown as a dialog and logged when the language is changed. {0} is a language name, already written in its own language - do not translate it. Deliberately one sentence ending in the placeholder: as "Language set to {0}. Restart the gateway to apply it." the machine pass dropped the ". " that followed the placeholder, producing "espanolReinicie" and "cestinaObnovit" - two sentences run together. Keep the placeholder at the end.

data.name: DlgAlreadyRunning
data.comment: Shown when a second copy is launched. The product name stays in English.

data.name: DlgUdpPortInvalid
data.value: The UDP listening port must be a whole number between 1 and 65535.

data.name: DlgMulticastInvalid
data.value:
{0}.
Leave this blank unless the sending program is configured to send to a multicast group.
data.comment: {0} is ErrNotAnIpAddress or ErrNotMulticast. Keep the blank line.

data.name: DlgNoFailedQsos
data.value:
Every QSO this session was delivered to DXKeeper.
{0} does not exist.
data.comment: {0} is a full file path - do not translate it.

data.name: DlgCouldNotOpenFile
data.comment: {0} is a filename, {1} is an operating-system error message. Do not translate either.

data.name: DlgCouldNotOpenFolder
data.comment: {0} is an operating-system error message - do not translate it.

data.name: DlgNoErrorLog
data.value:
Nothing has been written to the error log yet:
{0}
data.comment: {0} is the full path of ErrorLog.txt - do not translate it.

data.name: DlgCouldNotOpenErrorLog
data.comment: "ErrorLog.txt" is a filename - do not translate it. {0} is an operating-system error message.

data.name: DlgCouldNotOpenHelp
data.value:
Could not open the help page:
{0}
data.comment: {0} is an operating-system error message - do not translate it.

data.name: ErrNotAnIpAddress
data.value: "{0}" is not a valid IP address
data.comment: {0} is what the operator typed. Used inside DlgMulticastInvalid and AlertMulticastRejected, so it is a fragment, not a sentence - no full stop.

data.name: ErrNotMulticast
data.value: "{0}" is not an IPv4 multicast address (224.0.0.0 - 239.255.255.255)
data.comment: Fragment, no full stop. Do not translate the address range or "IPv4".

data.name: MsgBindFailed
data.value: Could not listen on UDP port {0}: {1}
data.comment: Used both as a dialog and as a log line. {0} is a port number, {1} is an operating-system error message.

data.name: AlertMulticastRejected
data.comment: {0} is ErrNotAnIpAddress or ErrNotMulticast. The emphasis on "without" matters: the gateway looks healthy but would receive nothing from that group.

data.name: AlertMulticastReverted
data.comment: {0} may be empty, meaning no multicast.

data.name: AlertUploadAlreadySent
data.value: Uploads are switched on, so {0} may already be at an online logbook. That upload cannot be undone, and this change does not reach it.
data.comment: Logged when a QSO is edited or deleted while any upload toggle is on. {0} describes the QSO. "may already be" is deliberate - the QSO was only uploaded if it was logged while the toggle was on, which this program cannot know for certain.

data.name: AlertReplaceNoKey
data.value: contactreplace for {0}: no usable <oldcall>/<oldtimestamp> - the edit was NOT applied to DXKeeper
data.comment: "contactreplace", "<oldcall>" and "<oldtimestamp>" are wire-format names - do not translate them. {0} is a callsign.

data.name: AlertDeleteNoKey
data.value: contactdelete for {0}: missing callsign or timestamp - nothing was sent to DXKeeper
data.comment: "contactdelete" is a wire-format name - do not translate it. {0} is a callsign.

data.name: AlertInternalError
data.value: INTERNAL ERROR handling a message. {0}: {1}. See ErrorLog.txt. The gateway is still running.
data.comment: A defect in this program, not bad input. {0} is an exception type name and {1} its message - do not translate either. The last sentence matters: it tells the operator not to restart mid-contest.

data.name: AlertInvalidMessage
data.comment: {0} describes what was wrong with a received datagram and stays in English - it is wire diagnostics that also goes to ErrorLog.txt.

data.name: AlertReplaceLostQso
data.value: *** {0}: DXKeeper DELETED the original but did not log the edit{1} - the edited QSO is in {2}, import it. Reason: {3}
data.comment: The most serious message this program emits: DXKeeper no longer holds the QSO at all. Keep the *** marker. {0} callsign, {1} an optional " (TCP 52001)" tag, {2} a filename, {3} a reason from the Fail* strings.

data.name: AlertReplaceLostQsoNotSaved
data.value: *** {0}: DXKeeper DELETED the original, the edit was not logged{1}, AND the edit could not be saved to {2}. Reason: {3}
data.comment: As AlertReplaceLostQso, but the recovery file could not be written either - the QSO is unrecoverable. Keep the *** marker.

data.name: AlertNotConfirmed
data.comment: {0} a short description of the QSO, {1} an optional " (TCP 52001)" tag, {2} AlertSavedTo or AlertNotSavedTo or empty, {3} a reason from the Fail* strings.

data.name: AlertSavedTo
data.comment: Fragment appended inside AlertNotConfirmed. Keep the leading space. {0} is a filename.

data.name: AlertNotSavedTo
data.value: - AND it could not be saved to {0}
data.comment: Fragment appended inside AlertNotConfirmed. Keep the leading space. {0} is a filename.

data.name: FailBusy
data.value: another send had not finished yet
data.comment: Deliberately plain. This read "another send was already in flight" and machine-translated into German as a literal statement about aviation - see the note on idioms at the top of this file.

data.name: FailConnectTimeout
data.value: the connection to DXKeeper timed out after {0} seconds
data.comment: {0} is a number of seconds.

data.name: FailConnectRefused
data.value: cannot connect to DXKeeper on TCP port {0}; in DXKeeper, check that {1} reports "Listening"
data.comment: {0} is a port number. {1} is DxKeeperConfigNetworkService, an English menu path inside DXKeeper - it must stay untranslated because DXKeeper's own interface is English-only.

data.name: FailNoPeerClose
data.value: DXKeeper never closed the connection within {0} seconds, so the QSO may never have been accepted
data.comment: {0} is a number of seconds. DXKeeper acknowledges only by closing the connection, so no close means the QSO cannot be claimed as delivered.

data.name: FailShuttingDown
data.value: the gateway was shutting down and this was never sent

data.name: FailSendFailed
data.comment: Last-resort wording when no more specific reason is available.

data.name: TranslatedBy
data.comment: WHOEVER TRANSLATED THIS FILE: replace this value with your name and callsign, however you would like to be credited. It is shown in the About window to anyone running the gateway in this language, and it is the one entry here that is not a translation of the English. Free-form - a name, a callsign, an email, a club, whatever you prefer. It is never overwritten by the machine-translation tool.

data.name: AboutLink
data.comment: Small link in the window footer that opens the About window.

data.name: AboutTitle
data.comment: Title of the About window. The product name stays in English.

data.name: AboutVersion
data.comment: {0} is a version number such as 2.0.0.

data.name: AboutPurpose
data.value: Carries QSOs from TR4W and N1MM Logger+ into DXKeeper, and asks DXView and Pathfinder about the callsigns you work.
data.comment: One-line description. All five product names stay in English. TR4W is named here and nowhere else - the program's title stays "N1MM-DXKeeper Gateway", which is what operators have called it for years.

data.name: AboutLicenceShort
data.value: Free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later, with ABSOLUTELY NO WARRANTY.

data.name: AboutTranslationBy
data.comment: {0} is a language name in its own language, {1} is the value of TranslatedBy. Do not translate either.

data.name: AboutOriginal
data.value: A rewrite of the original VB6 gateway. The DXLab Suite message formats are the work of AA6YQ.
data.comment: "VB6", "DXLab Suite" and the callsign AA6YQ stay in English.

data.name: AboutCopyProfile
data.comment: Button that copies version and environment details to the clipboard for pasting into a bug report.

data.name: NoticeTitle
data.comment: Title of the first-run notice window. Deliberately not "Licence Agreement" - nothing is being agreed to.

data.name: NoticeFreeSoftware
data.value: N1MM-DXKeeper Gateway is free software under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or later. You may use it for any purpose, study how it works, share it, and change it.
data.comment: "GNU General Public License" is the name of a licence - do not translate it.

data.name: NoticeWarranty
data.value: It comes with ABSOLUTELY NO WARRANTY. It is offered in the hope that it is useful, but nobody guarantees it is fit for any particular purpose, and no contributor is liable for anything that goes wrong. Your log is your responsibility: check that QSOs reach DXKeeper.
data.comment: The point of this window. Keep the emphasis on "no warranty" - many languages capitalise for emphasis differently, so use whatever reads as emphatic. The last sentence is specific to this program: the operator's contest log is at stake.

data.name: NoticeWhereToFind
data.value: The full licence is in the file COPYING.txt next to the program, and is always available from the About link in the window.
data.comment: "COPYING.txt" is a filename - do not translate it.

data.name: NoticeViewLicence
data.comment: Button that opens the COPYING file.

data.name: NoticeUnderstood
data.comment: Button that dismisses the notice. An acknowledgement, not an acceptance - see the note above.

data.name: DlgCouldNotOpenLicence
data.value:
Could not open the licence file:
{0}
data.comment: {0} is an operating-system error message - do not translate it.

data.name: DlgLicenceMissing
data.comment: Shown when COPYING is missing next to the program - a broken install. {0} is a file path. Do not translate the URL or the licence name.

data.name: TrayShow
data.comment: Notification area menu entry that brings the window back. Also the double-click action. Phrased as a full instruction rather than "Show gateway", which machine-translated into German as "Schaufenster" (a shop window) - a bare verb-noun pair gives a translator nothing to disambiguate against.

data.name: TrayQuit
data.comment: Notification area menu entry that shuts the gateway down. Not the bare word "Quit", which machine-translated into German as "Quittung" (a receipt), Japanese as "login" and Korean as nonsense. Naming the object gives the model something to work with.

data.name: TrayHiddenTitle
data.comment: Title of the notification shown the first time the window is minimised to the notification area.

data.name: TrayHiddenMessage
data.value: The gateway is still receiving QSOs here. Double-click this icon to bring the window back.
data.comment: Shown once per session. It matters: an operator who thinks they closed the gateway would stop watching for problems while it is still the only thing logging their contest.

data.name: TrayReceived
data.comment: Count of UDP datagrams received. Menu entry.

data.name: TrayLogged
data.comment: Count of QSOs DXKeeper confirmed. Menu entry.

data.name: TrayQueued
data.comment: Count of QSOs queued behind the one in flight. Menu entry.

data.name: TrayNotDelivered
data.comment: Count of QSOs DXKeeper did not confirm. Menu entry. The emphasis is deliberate - this is the number that needs acting on.

data.name: TrayAllDelivered
data.comment: Menu entry shown instead of TrayNotDelivered when nothing has failed.

data.name: TrayLastQso
data.comment: {0} is a callsign and time, e.g. "W1AW 14:32". Menu entry.

data.name: TrayOpenFailedFile
data.comment: Menu entry that opens FailedQSOs_*.adi.

data.name: TrayOpenFailedFolder
data.comment: Menu entry that opens Explorer with the undelivered-QSO file selected. Needed as well as the entry above because .adi often has no program associated with it, and because the file may not be in the Gateway's own folder.

data.name: TrayFailureTitle
data.comment: Title of the notification raised when DXKeeper does not confirm a QSO while the window is hidden.

data.name: TrayFailureMessage
data.value: DXKeeper has not confirmed {0} QSOs this session. They are saved for you to import by hand.
data.comment: {0} is a count. Raised while the window is hidden, because the operator cannot see the warning bar then.

data.name: TrayTooltip
data.comment: Tooltip under the product name. Windows caps the whole tooltip at 127 characters and it is truncated past that, so keep this short.

data.name: DxKeeperConfigNetworkService
data.comment: DO NOT TRANSLATE. A literal menu path inside DXKeeper, whose interface is English-only.
